title: Reduce secrets blast radius: staged sealedsecret promotion + envelope-key fallback
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Introduce staged promotion of sealed secrets and envelope-key fallback for zero-downtime TLS rekeying; Terraform module bump for kms_key_binding_v2; Helm hooks to ensure idempotent pre-upgrade secret staging; rollback path documented.
description: Context: customer installs running Redwood Private in regulated VPCs required a safer TLS rekey path that avoids broad sealedsecret replacements and supports gradual cutover with an HSM-backed envelope key fallback. Motivation: previous bulk-rotation workflows caused transient downtime and increased ops toil when controllers re-applied long-lived sealed secrets across namespaces. This PR implements a staged promotion workflow plus an envelope-key fallback that reduces blast radius, supports dry-run promotion, and enables safe rollback. Design summary: 1) Add a new 'staged-seal' Helm subchart that creates promotion artifacts in a dedicated namespace (redwood-seal-staging) and ties to a new Kubernetes Job pre-upgrade hook that validates the promotion on a small sample of workloads; 2) Extend the terraform 'kms_key_binding' module to v2 which emits an envelope-key ARN and a promotion flag; 3) Introduce a vault migration helper (cli script) that migrates existing sealed secrets into the staged namespace by re-encrypting with the envelope key while leaving original secrets intact; 4) Implement controller-side gating so the private-installer controller only flips production references after an explicit 'promote' annotation applied to the staging object; 5) Add metrics (staging.promotions_total, staging.failures_total) and tracing spans for each promotion step. Migration plan: - Default deploys create staging artifacts but do not promote; operators run the included dry-run job which validates decryption and TLS chain rotation for one ingress per namespace; - After SMT validation, operator annotates the 'staged-seal' resource to trigger canary promotion across a subset of namespaces; - Full promotion requires two successful canaries spaced 30 minutes apart. Rollback plan: annotated reversal flips references back to original sealed secrets; envelope key remains available for decrypting any promoted items until an operator executes a safe purge command. Helm/Terraform changes: - Helm: new subchart 'staged-seal' with templates/sealed-promote-job.yaml (pre-upgrade hook), templates/secret-proxy.yaml, and Chart.yaml bump; add hookweight/annotations to ensure deterministic ordering during upgrades; - Terraform: module kms_key_binding v2 with new output envelope_key_arn, input enable_promotion boolean and migration helpers; state migration script included as scripts/tf-state-backcompat.sh; - Installer: add CLI flags --enable-staged-seal and --promotion-timeout to private-installer bootstrap command. Testing and validation: unit tests for helm templates, integration harness test that runs the dry-run job in kind with a mocked KMS (local kms emulator), e2e (gke) smoke test that performs a canary promotion then rollback. Security considerations: envelope-key usage is audited via new audit log entries and requires KMS Decrypt permission scoped to service account; promotion annotation is RBAC gated to cluster-admin by default; migration helper logs sensitive operations and can be run with --audit-only for planning. CI: add parallel pipeline stage 'staged-seal-smoke' that runs the kind-based dry-run. Observability: dashboards added in redwood-console-config (prometheus queries and alert rules for promotion failures).
